content:
Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to provide users with a way to transfer their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Here are the details.

iOS will make app replacement easier

While it doesn't happen often, developers sometimes remove an existing app and replace it with a new one, requiring users to switch to a separate, standalone app.

Although most developers try to make the transition seamless, the migration process may still require some action from users, particularly for data that isn't stored in the cloud.

With iOS 27.2, Apple will address this issue through a system-managed migration flow, allowing supported data and settings to be transferred to a designated replacement app before the old app is deleted.

Based on code currently visible in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see the following prompt:

"The developer suggests transferring your data and settings from your current "%1$@" app to the new "%2$@" app. Your iPhone can handle this for you before you start using the new app. When it's done, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone."

Users can choose to "Transfer App Data & Settings" or "Transfer Nothing." If a user declines the migration, iOS will show a second confirmation warning noting that some preferences — including notification and location settings — may need to be reconfigured.

It's worth noting that this feature appears to be limited to developers replacing their own apps with a designated replacement app, rather than migrating data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a range of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, location, and health authorization decisions
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • App-specific Do Not Disturb and Focus Mode settings
  • App Lock and protection settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and accessory Live Activities
  • Access to related accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, camera-related defaults, phone data, and Secure Element services

We'll be keeping a close eye on updates to this framework throughout the iOS 27.2 beta testing period, and will report back when we learn more about how developers implement this feature.
